scope: Original token compilation and custom-property substitution against supplied winning element snapshots. No actual cascade, CSSOM, layout, rendering, JS, network, GPU, UI or Chrome performance evidence.
method: Three CPU-0 sequential alternating cold/warm runs, reversed in the middle. 2000 compiles per prebuilt value and 20000 resolutions for ordinary cases, 40 for large expansion/repeated-cycle cases. Cold control clears results before each request but retains worker capacities; warm retains property results. Both memoize within a request. Summaries are medians of three run means; first-call samples recorded separately, including resolver construction. Batch control separately compiles/drops 1000 values independently or in one arena, repeated 20 times per run.
cycle_method: Three sequential alternating corrected suffix-scan control/default runs, cold mode. Only mark_cycle differs: earlier suffix min/mark scans versus root selection from first guard and already-marked suffix check. Same benchmark and limit/taint/cycle semantics; all supported fixtures/generated graphs pass with the corrected suffix-scan algorithm.
common_method: Three sequential alternating parent/default runs for unchanged CSS and color benchmarks, reversed in the middle; CSS 5 rounds, color 20. Parent built from exact HEAD module exports with new modules excluded, restored in finally; all other reachable production files and benchmark sources match HEAD. These common paths have no intended algorithm change.
caveats: No concurrent checks launched by this session during samples. Other machine load, clocks, thermals, hash seeds and allocator/code layout uncontrolled.
Prebuilt Syntax excludes lexical/source costs in variables_bench. Common CSS benchmark separately includes its original syntax workload.
Cold/warm are API usage controls of one implementation, not previous production revisions; the old engine had no variable resolver.
Compile timings across cache modes vary despite identical compilation code; do not attribute that variance to memoization.

Retained arena accounting includes unique shared inputs/program headers/source/node/dimension capacities; excludes allocator and hash-table/control/guard metadata. Count each shared arena once, not once per view/clone.

One view retains its whole batch. The benchmark freezes its entire input snapshot and retains the first returned value during its timing loop. RSS includes those inputs, outputs/pools and allocator retention; not browser/page memory.
No new SIMD or GPU implementation here; string copies use Rust/native memory primitives and the original bounded token machinery.
Common-path variation is not a uniform improvement or regression guarantee.
